summary: The Strategy Lab architecture is SHADOW-safe and cross-chain-governed, but the hourly review inputs would be more durable with recency-aware scorecards and freshness metadata. Fresh runtime evidence is stale, so this cycle cannot justify profitability or live-readiness claims.

evidence.detail: strategy_metrics() aggregates all stored strategy_lab_windows rows for a strategy, and evaluate_strategy() uses those lifetime totals to drive REWORK/REPLACE/PROMOTION_CANDIDATE decisions.
build_loss_forensics_with_strategy_lab() calls portfolio_report(app) inside the hourly export path, so the hourly review inherits lifetime-aggregate decisioning.
The hourly review specification expects reviewers to judge which strategies generated opportunities, participated, and made or lost money after costs in the reviewed evidence window.

proposals.rationale: Lifetime aggregation can mask regime shifts. A previously good strategy can continue to look strong after recent deterioration, and a recovering strategy can remain buried under old losses. For hourly durable-net-P&L review, recent/trailing evidence should be visible alongside lifetime totals.
proposals.expected_effect: Reduce stale-history bias in REWORK/REPLACE/PROMOTION_CANDIDATE calls by adding recent per-chain trailing-window performance and participation views next to the lifetime baseline.
proposals.downside_risk: Short recency windows can under-sample quiet but valid strategies, so recent slices should complement rather than replace the lifetime scorecard.
proposals.shadow_test: For each strategy and chain, compare lifetime-only decisions versus decisions that also require positive trailing net P&L and profit factor on recent windows such as 3/24/72-hour slices. Keep the change only if forward shadow review reduces stale-candidate reversals without reducing participation in newly profitable opportunities.
proposals.minimum_observation: At least 3 recent windows and 8 trades per reviewed strategy-chain slice before using recency-aware promotion or replacement signals.

proposals.strategy: Recency and dispersion metadata for research cohorts

evidence.detail: profitable_wallet_research() ranks positive wallets by aggregate net/profit factor and learned_pattern_portability() ranks classes by replicability, but neither report includes last-seen timestamps, recent-window counts, or recent-vs-historical dispersion.
sibot_observed_wallet_learning() returns timestamps for recent copy recommendations, but behaviour_rankings and copy_wallet_candidates omit freshness fields in the sanitised summary.
The seeded internal-learning tables include updated_at data, yet the report contract currently validates anonymisation and research-only behavior rather than freshness propagation.

proposals.rationale: When fresh runtime evidence is unavailable, research cohorts need explicit freshness and dispersion metadata so the reviewer can distinguish durable multi-window behavior from stale all-time winners and avoid overweighting a single historical regime.
proposals.expected_effect: Improve confidence calibration for new SHADOW hypotheses by surfacing whether supporting wallets, patterns, and behaviors are recent, repeated, and stable across more than one window or regime.
proposals.downside_risk: Additional metadata increases report size and can down-rank infrequent but real edges if freshness thresholds are applied too mechanically.
proposals.shadow_test: Add recent-window counts, last-seen timestamps, and dispersion summaries to cohort outputs, then compare whether hypotheses generated from freshness-aware cohorts produce better next-window net P&L and fewer false-positive proposals than hypotheses generated from all-time aggregates alone.
proposals.minimum_observation: At least 3 observation windows or equivalent recent-count and last-seen evidence for each cited wallet cohort, learned pattern, or SiBot behavior before elevating it to a new cross-chain hypothesis.

rejected_ideas.idea: Claim profitability, canary readiness, or live readiness from this cycle alone.
rejected_ideas.reason: Fresh runtime evidence within 2h is false, so architecture inspection can guide SHADOW research but cannot prove current live edge.

rejected_ideas.idea: Port a single-chain profitable-wallet or learned-pattern signal directly to both chains without separate executable quote, liquidity, sellability, and cost validation.
rejected_ideas.reason: Cross-chain governance explicitly requires chain-specific execution and cost assumptions and forbids inferring live readiness from one chain's results alone.

evidence_gaps: Fresh runtime evidence within 2h is false, so this review cannot claim current profitability, canary readiness, or live readiness.

The repository snapshot available for review does not contain the raw sanitised evidence package bytes for this cycle, only the exact source commit and evidence SHA-256 metadata, so findings are limited to source-architecture inspection and documented governance paths.
